speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly where the swelling is located in your right knee, and how would you describe the pain if I pressed on the joint line? Additionally, have you noticed any recent episodes of the knee suddenly locking or giving way?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (oligoarticular) with a possible genetic predisposition. Given the patient's age, insidious onset after minor activity, and family history, this is the most likely etiology despite the lack of acute trauma. I recommend requesting a Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) to check for systemic inflammation. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR.
